thread.title: Tech Today: Alphabet's New High, Prepping Apple Models, Verizon Rising - Nasdaq.com

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: Alphabet's New High, Prepping Apple Models, Verizon Rising - Nasdaq.com
text:
Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Alphabet's New High
Shares of Alphabet ( GOOGL ) are up $47.67, or almost 4%, to $1258.67, after the company yesterday afternoon reported Q2 revenue and profit that topped analysts' expectations.
The stock reached a new all-time high earlier of $1,275.
Price targets are zooming into the $1,400-plus range this morning at many shops.
Mizuho 's James Lee reiterates a Buy rating on the stock, and raises his target to $1,460 from $1,350, noting that the Google unit's revenue from its owned websites keyword search was better than he expected, up 24%, year-over-year, excluding the impact of the higher dollar.
However, while the number of "paid clicks" was "solid," up 58%, pricing was weaker than he expected, down 25%.
He notes, too, that cloud computing boosted Google's " Other " line of revenue, driving the revenue growth rate to 43%, a 7-point increase.
Verizon's Wireless Strength
Shares of Verizon Communications ( VZ ) are up 38 cents, or 0.8%, to $51.13, after the company this morning reported Q2 revenue and earnings that topped consensus, delivering $32.2 billion in revenue and $1.20 earnings per share, versus consensus estimates for revenue of $31.78 billion and EPS of $1.15.
The company also raised its revenue growth outlook from "from low-single-digits percentage growth to mid-of-single-digits."
Verizon said it added 531,000 post-paid wireless network subscribers on a "net" basis.
CEO Lowell McAdam called the results "strong," "as evidenced by service revenue, earnings and operating cash flow growth delivered in a highly competitive marketplace."
Jennifer Fritzsche with Wells Fargo , who has an Outperform rating on the shares, writes that it was "a very solid print for VZ, particularly in its wireless business where service revenues, postpaid phone net adds and postpaid ARPA (average revenue per account) came in well ahead of expectations."
She notes Verizon "appears to also be benefiting from customers stepping up to higher priced wireless plans and increasing average connections per account."
"Wireline margins and video net losses came in slightly shy of our estimates, although this isn't overly surprising as VZ has been focusing more on its wireless business."
Ams Fails to Lift Fiber-Optic Names
Of note to investors in fiber-optic component stocks, the report yesterday by Ams Ag ( AMS ) of Q2 results should be giving a lifting to optical names, though it's not.
The company, which makes parts used in " 3-D sensing " functions, including for Apple 's ( AAPL ) iPhone , said that it sees "major ramps in consumer optical sensing underway," and projected this quarter's revenue to be up sharply, by 46% to 59%.
That's not helping the big players in optical today, whose shares have been under a cloud in the past week after a supplier to Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ), WIN Semiconductor ( 3105TW ), warned it expects revenue will be lower than the company previously expected in the second half of this year, implicating Lumentum's parts for 3-D sensing.
Despite Ams's positive read on things, shares of Lumentum are down $1.62, or 3%, to $52.78. Shares of competitor Finisar (FNSR) are unchanged at $16.77.
Ams stock is up 2 cents, or half a percent, on the Swiss exchange, to 2.96 Swiss francs.
Get Your iPhone Models Ready
Speaking of Apple, analysts continue to refine their models for what to look for next Tuesday, July 31 , when the company is expected to report fiscal Q3 results after the closing bell.
Toni Sacconaghi of Bernstein today reiterates a Market Perform rating on Apple shares, writing that investors will be all over the hints of the next iPhone , the one presumably coming in September, asking questions such as " what might Apple charge for the new models? " "how many units might Apple sell?" and "what might gross margins be?"
Morgan Stanley 's Katy Huberty has a few thoughts on that matter.
She reiterates an Overweight rating on the stock, and raises her price target to $232 from $214, writing that Apple will probably deliver an "in-line June quarter and provide a slightly weaker-than-consensus September quarter outlook due to a possible October launch of the 6.1" LCD iPhone .
"We currently see no delay in the ramp of Apple's upcoming flagship 5.8" or 6.5" OLED iPhones, however suspected issues with LED backlight leakage have caused a 1 month delay in mass production of the 6.1" LCD iPhone, although this is down from a 6-week delay baked into the original production forecast, according to suppliers."
AT&T, TI Earnings Ahead
On tap for earnings this afternoon, after the closing bell, are AT&T (T), networking-component maker Inphi (IPHI), and analog-chip giant Texas Instruments (TXN).
